record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: Fix alpha,beta in (0,1) with alpha + beta = 1. For theta = (theta_1,theta_2), consider the set of shifts eta = (eta_1,eta_2) in R^2 for which inf over q of max(q^alpha ||q theta_1 - eta_1||, q^beta ||q theta_2 - eta_2||) is positive. Harrap proved that this shift set has full Hausdorff dimension when theta belongs to BAD(alpha,beta). Does the same full-Hausdorff-dimension statement, and even the Schmidt-game winning property, hold without assuming theta belongs to BAD(alpha,beta)?

evidence.quote: For α, β ∈ [0, 1] under the condition α + β = 1 and δ > 0 we consider the sets BAD(α, β; δ)

Harrap [57] proved that given α, β ∈ (0, 1), α + β = 1 for a fixed vector (θ1 , θ2 ) ∈ BAD(α, β) the set {(η1 , η2 ) ∈ R2 : inf max(q α ||qθ1 − η1 ||, q β ||qθ2 − η2 || > 0} has full Hausdorff dimension.
The following question formulated by Harrap [57]: to prove that the set (9) is a set of full Hausdorff dimension (and even a winning set) without the condition (8).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1)$ satisfy $\alpha+\beta=1$. For $q\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Define the weighted badly approximable set
$$\mathrm{BAD}(\alpha,\beta)=\Big\{(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:\inf_{q\in\mathbb{N}}\max\!\big(q^{\alpha}\|q\theta_1\|,\ q^{\beta}\|q\theta_2\|\big)>0\Big\}.$$
For a fixed $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, consider the shift set
$$S(\theta)=\Big\{(\eta_1,\eta_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:\inf_{q\in\mathbb{N}}\max\!\big(q^{\alpha}\|q\theta_1-\eta_1\|,\ q^{\beta}\|q\theta_2-\eta_2\|\big)>0\Big\}.$$
It is known that whenever $\theta\in\mathrm{BAD}(\alpha,\beta)$, the set $S(\theta)$ has full Hausdorff dimension $2$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Without the assumption $\theta\in\mathrm{BAD}(\alpha,\beta)$, is it true that for every $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^2$ (with $\theta_1,\theta_2$ irrational, say) the set $S(\theta)$ still has full Hausdorff dimension $2$? Moreover, is $S(\theta)$ a winning set for Schmidt's game?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turn up Harrap's original full-dimension result for $\theta\in\mathrm{BAD}(\alpha,\beta)$ and various subsequent advances on weighted/twisted inhomogeneous badly approximable sets (including winning properties on nondegenerate curves and inhomogeneous Schmidt's conjecture in arbitrary dimensions), but no source clearly resolves the full-dimension/winning question for arbitrary $\theta$ outside $\mathrm{BAD}(\alpha,\beta)$. Status remains unclear from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Twisted inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation and badly approximable sets
status_evidence.snippet: Bad^x(i,j), the twisted inhomogeneous analogue of Bad(i,j), has full Hausdorff dimension 2 when x is chosen from the set Bad(i,j).
status_evidence.claim: Original Harrap result requires theta in BAD(alpha,beta).

status_evidence.title: Weighted twisted inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation (arXiv:2307.13210)
status_evidence.snippet: Hausdorff dimension results for the weighted twisted inhomogeneous set.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses related weighted twisted inhomogeneous settings but does not clearly remove the BAD(alpha,beta) hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Winning of inhomogeneous bad for curves (arXiv:2309.02018)
status_evidence.snippet: absolute winning property of weighted inhomogeneous badly approximable vectors on nondegenerate analytic curves
status_evidence.claim: Winning results exist in related (curve) settings but not directly resolving the unconstrained-theta question.
